findings.requirement: The supplier shall compile all firmware user-space binaries with stack protection (-fstack-protector-strong or equivalent) and provide build-flag evidence with each release.
findings.acceptance_test: at least 90% of executables carry stack canaries
findings.rationale: Stack canaries detect linear stack buffer overflows (the bug class behind the TALOS-2019-0862 family of iocheckd issues) and turn exploitation into a crash.

checks.expected: all have canary, pie, relro_full, nx

findings.requirement: The supplier shall harden all network-exposed services with stack canaries, PIE, full RELRO and NX.
findings.acceptance_test: every network-facing daemon has canary, PIE, full RELRO and NX
findings.rationale: Network daemons are the remotely reachable attack surface; a missing mitigation there matters more than in a local CLI tool.

findings.requirement: The supplier shall ensure that no executable stack segments ship in the firmware.
findings.acceptance_test: 100% of executables have a non-executable stack
findings.rationale: An executable stack makes injected shellcode directly runnable.

findings.requirement: The supplier shall deliver a machine-readable SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX) with each release, covering at least 90 % of components with version and identifier (purl or CPE).
findings.acceptance_test: at least 90% of SBOM components have a version and a purl/CPE
findings.rationale: Without an identified component inventory, vulnerability management is guesswork (SM-9 mapping to be confirmed).

findings.requirement: The supplier shall ship no known critical or actively exploited vulnerabilities in third-party components at delivery, or provide a VEX statement justifying non-exploitability.
findings.acceptance_test: no more than 0 critical and 0 KEV-listed CVEs
findings.rationale: Critical and actively exploited CVEs are the most likely entry points in the field.

findings.requirement: The supplier shall remediate high-severity CVEs in network-facing components within an agreed SLA (e.g. 90 days).
findings.acceptance_test: no more than 5 critical/high CVEs in network-facing components
findings.rationale: Network-facing components are reachable without local access.

observed.name: linux
observed.reason: Linux kernels before 5.10 are past upstream end of life

observed.name: openssl
observed.reason: OpenSSL 1.x is past end of life (1.1.1 ended 2023-09-11)

findings.requirement: The supplier shall not ship components past upstream end-of-life without a documented support arrangement.
findings.acceptance_test: no end-of-life components (e.g. OpenSSL 1.x, pre-5.10 kernels)
findings.rationale: End-of-life components no longer receive security fixes.

findings.requirement: The supplier shall provide a signed SHA-256 digest manifest for every firmware release before site commissioning.
findings.acceptance_test: a vendor signature or signed digest accompanies the image
findings.rationale: The asset owner needs a way to verify that the image is the one the vendor released.

findings.requirement: The device shall verify the authenticity and integrity of firmware updates before installation.
findings.acceptance_test: a signature-verifying update mechanism is present (e.g. RAUC keyring)
findings.rationale: Unsigned updates let anyone with network access replace the firmware.

findings.requirement: The supplier shall document and enable boot-integrity protection (signed FIT, dm-verity or secure boot).
findings.rationale: Without boot integrity, a modified root filesystem persists across reboots.

findings.requirement: Clear-text management services (Telnet, FTP, TFTP, rsh, HTTP) shall be disabled by default.
findings.acceptance_test: no clear-text services enabled by default
findings.rationale: Clear-text protocols expose credentials and commands on the plant network.

findings.requirement: The device shall force a change of default credentials at first use and store password hashes with a modern KDF.
findings.acceptance_test: no empty, weakly hashed or documented default passwords
findings.rationale: Documented default passwords are the first thing an attacker tries.

findings.requirement: Unique key material shall be generated per device at provisioning; no private keys shall be shipped in the firmware image.
findings.acceptance_test: no private keys in the image
findings.rationale: A key shipped in the image is shared by every device and can be extracted from the download.
